report: Independently reassessed the complete claim and the one ordinary parser implementation / one ordinary annotated test; no TODO or N/A entries. Historical parser.rs and language.rs snapshots exactly match current files. Triple-quoted tokenization preserves the text, optional_prose consumes it when present, and type_declaration reads it immediately after a tuple or named payload opener, or after a unit variant name. Each enum-loop iteration creates and stores its own description in a new Variant, independent of surrounding declaration and other variants. The complete parses_structs_enums_and_opaque_generics test supplies all three placements and directly asserts the distinct exact retained strings for Never, Tuple, and Ref as well as the separate enum description and correct payload forms. These assertions would detect rejected placements, dropped prose, or cross-variant contamination. Optional absence is supported by optional_prose returning None; the claim promises the supported prose placements rather than an exhaustive grammar restriction. All necessary parser helpers are present in the captured whole parser file; no external behavioral helper was needed for the direct parse/result assertions. This is source inspection and exact historical comparison; I ran review start/read/record, not behavioral tests or a build. Coordinator-reported test/build results are separate evidence. No edits are needed.
